evidence.quote: St. Gaudens himself was in Paris, putting on the work his usual interminable last touches
which had been given the central post of honor. Of all the American artists
Once St. Gaudens took him down to Amiens to see the cathedral.

Adams enjoyed
lecturing Augustus St. Gaudens

adjudications.reason: The revision never says that St. Gaudens is in Paris. Paragraph 15 mentions only his statue in the art exhibit and then his temperament, so 'Once St. Gaudens took him down to Amiens' lacks a stated physical presence. Their friendship is already known from chapter 023, where Adams lectures St. Gaudens and has the Rock Creek figure. That makes the full studio paragraph unnecessary. Restoring the single source sentence placing him in Paris is enough to ground the excursion.
